Subject: POC day: runbook & structured-output readiness / finalize kickoff slot

Hi Amit / Lina —

Thanks again for agreeing to run the hands-on POC with Redwood. To make the day productive we want to lock the kickoff slot (30–45m) followed by a 3-hour lab window for prompt review, routing checks, and a light load test.

Proposed kickoff times (PDT):
- Option A: Thu Aug 26 — 11:00–11:45
- Option B: Fri Aug 27 — 09:30–10:15

Please confirm which works better and whether you want the runbook circulated in advance. High-level asks from our side so we can prepare:
- Prompt inventory (sample prompts + any expected structured-output fields)
- Expected concurrency / peak users for a 15-min load test (requests per second)
- Any routing rules (region/priority user groups) and guardrails we should enforce for the workshop

I attached a short runbook draft (runbook_day0.pdf) that shows timings, owner assignments, and rollback/fallback steps. Ben — can you add the load-test plan once Amit confirms expected concurrency? Priyom / Marissa — will coordinate monitoring, SLIs, and notifications.

Goal for the POC day: validate prompt conformance to a JSON schema-like output, verify routing fallback to a lower-cost model under load, and measure 95th percentile latency for 2048-token sessions.

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.

Best,
Jonas
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: POC day: runbook & structured-output readiness / finalize kickoff slot

Thanks Jonas — building on this. A few quick technical clarifications from engineering: 

1) For the load test we need an estimate of peak concurrent sessions and rough request patterns (burst vs steady). If you expect short bursts (e.g., 400 requests in 1–2 minutes) say so; otherwise give a steady-rps number.

2) For structured output validation, do you want us to enforce a strict JSON schema (fail the request) or do soft validation and log regressions? We usually recommend soft validation for first run and a canary policy.

3) If you plan to route by customer tier or workspace, please list the routing keys. We'll pre-create routing rules and a fallback mapping to the verified-compact model.

I'll draft the load_test_plan.md and attach a stub for the POC. Once Amit confirms the RPS target I'll finish the command list and a single-line curl harness you can run locally.

-Ben
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: load_test_plan.md (Markdown stub)

From: Amit Rao <amit.rao@stratusai.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lina Park <lina.park@carahtech.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-21T14:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC day: runbook & structured-output readiness / finalize kickoff slot

Jonas — thanks. Option A (Thu Aug 26, 11:00 PDT) is best for our team. Confirmed attendees: myself (lead product), Lina (integration lead), plus one ML engineer (Sofia, on the thread but OOO until Monday — she'll join the lab if needed).

Answers inline:
- Prompt inventory: attaching a CSV with ~28 representative prompts and a sample desired JSON output column (prompt_inventory.csv). The structured fields we care about are: intent (string), entities (list of {type,value}), confidence (float), canonical_text (string).
- Load characteristics: expecting a short demo burst for customers — estimate 250 requests over a 3-minute surge (~1.4 RPS average during the surge) and otherwise 5–10 RPS steady. For safety please plan for a 20 RPS headroom.
- Routing: We want routing by workspace_id and a fallback for unknown workspaces to "shared-low-priority".
- Validation: prefer soft validation (log + flag regressions) for the first run; if we pass conformance checks in the next sprint we can move to strict enforcement.

Please confirm you can run the 3-hour lab window starting 11:30 right after kickoff and include the guardrail checklist (rate limits, explicit token caps, allowed tools). Also include a short schema example in the runbook.

—Amit
VP Product, StratusAI

Attachments: prompt_inventory.csv (CSV, 12 KB)
